metaDescription: CPT 99490 explained: the base monthly CCM code. Time threshold, documentation, consent, who can perform it, the 2026 rate and common audit gaps.
summary: The base monthly Chronic Care Management code. It pays for the first 20 minutes of clinical staff time spent coordinating care for a patient with two or more chronic conditions, under the billing practitioner's direction.
time: 20 minutes of clinical staff time per calendar month
performer: Clinical staff under the billing practitioner's direction
frequency: Once per patient per calendar month, by one practitioner
requirements: Two or more chronic conditions expected to last at least 12 months or until death, with significant risk of decline
Documented patient consent (verbal or written) covering cost sharing and the right to stop
A comprehensive care plan in the record, shared with the patient or caregiver
A time log showing minutes, who performed them and what was done
24/7 access to the care team and continuity with a designated team member
pitfalls: Billing before the 20-minute threshold is reached; minutes do not roll into next month
Missing or undated consent, the most common audit gap
Two practitioners billing CCM for the same patient in the same month
Counting time that was already part of a separately billed visit
conflicts: Not reported in the same month as 99487 or 99491 by the same practitioner for the same patient.

faqs.question: What is the minimum time to bill CPT 99490?
faqs.answer: Twenty minutes of qualifying clinical staff time in the calendar month. Anything under that is not reportable and does not carry over.

faqs.question: Can the same patient be billed 99490 by two practices?
faqs.answer: No. Only one practitioner can bill CCM for a patient in a given month, so confirm no other practice is already billing before you enroll.

faqs.question: Does Zenith bill 99490 to Medicare?
faqs.answer: No. Your practice bills the code. Zenith supplies the clinical staff time and invoices your practice for the labor.
